Cellwise weighted maximum likelihood scatter of the residuals

Source: R/imputeCellGLoc.R
dot-gloc_scatter_soft.Rd

Uses cellWise::cwLocScat() when available. cellWise is in Suggests, so its absence is a supported configuration rather than an edge case; the fallback is a weighted pairwise covariance, which still honours the cell weights, and it is never taken silently.

.gloc_scatter_soft(
  R,
  W,
  M,
  kappa = 1,
  crit = 1e-08,
  have_cw = requireNamespace("cellWise", quietly = TRUE),
  em = FALSE
)

Arguments

R

\(n x p\) matrix of residuals from the mean structure.

W

\(n x p\) matrix of cell weights in [0, 1].

M

\(n x p\) logical mask of missing cells.

kappa

Gaussian consistency factor to divide by; see .gloc_consistency.

crit

convergence tolerance handed to cellWise::cwLocScat's EM. This is an inner loop inside the outer cellGLoc iteration, and it is the whole cost of a cellGLoc step: about 95% of an iteration against about 5% for the conditional residuals. Measured by Rprof over five draws at \(n = 1000\), \(p = 10\), \(\rho = 0.5\), 5% of cells shifted by +8, weights = "soft", across design = ~ 1 and design = ~ .: the share runs 94.3 to 95.6%. Earlier releases quoted 98.8% here and 97.5% elsewhere for the same quantity; neither reproduced, and 95% replaces both. cwLocScat's own default is 1e-12, seven orders of magnitude tighter than the outer loop's eps of 5e-3 can resolve, so the EM spends most of its steps refining digits the caller discards. The default 1e-8 is still five orders tighter than the outer tolerance; measured on \(n = 1000, p = 10\) it changed the scatter by 1.5e-9 in absolute value and cut the scatter step's time by about 30%.

have_cw

whether cellWise may be used; exposed so the fallback path is directly testable.

em

whether the rows are the categorical EM's pseudo-rows, whose cell weights carry a level's posterior probability. TRUE stops instead of falling back; see the note above.

Value

a \(p x p\) scatter matrix.

Details

The fallback is refused under em = TRUE. cwLocScat turns a row's cell weights into a case weight linearly, which is what lets the categorical EM weight a pseudo-row by its level's posterior probability; the fallback forms pairwise weights \(w_{ij} w_{ik}\) instead, so scaling a row by \(r\) scales its contribution by \(r^2\) and a row split evenly over two levels would count 0.25 + 0.25 against a complete row's 1. That is a silent statistical error rather than a cruder estimator, so this stops.
